content:
Just came across a pretty annoying issue; we can't tag anything with AntisymmRel because AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) a b gets turned into AntisymmRel (· ≥ ·) a b.

I think the standard fix would be to implement a new def for AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) and make it its own dual, but I'd like to go one step further. Why do we even have the relation argument? Is there anywhere in Mathlib where we genuinely need this generality?
You mean Preorder? In a partial order, AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) a b is the same as a = b.
My proposal is to write AntisymmRel a b for what we currently write as AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) a b
And then we can tell to_dual that this definition is its own dual, and all's good.

That sounds reasonable to me.

Any potential downstream users of AntisymmRel that use a different relation should be able to adapt by simply inlining its definition (AntisymmRel (a b : α) := r a b ∧ r b a). For example in

/-- The valuation equals relation, defined as `x =ᵥ y ↔ x ≤ᵥ y ∧ y ≤ᵥ x`. -/
def veq : R → R → Prop := AntisymmRel (· ≤ᵥ ·)
For consistency, I think IncompRel should get the same refactor. Though it seems that IncompRel is unused in mathlib.
I was the one who added veq and yeah I agree with inlining it there.
IncompRel does see some small use in the CGT repo, only ever with the ≤ relation on games
I should probably @Yaël Dillies since they are a coauthor of the antisymmetrization file

It is a bit dissatisfying that there are a bunch of other relations of this form (e.g. in Mathlib.Logic.Relation) which also take a relation as an argument. But some of those are genuinely used in full generality. So why don't we want to have AntisymmRel in full generality?
Well, the reason I raise the issue is that to_dual can't properly dualize it, since it tries to dualize AntisymmRel (· ≤ ·) to AntisymmRel (· ≥ ·).
And if we don't need the full generality then specializing this definition to Preorder and tagging it as its own dual seems like the easiest solution.
Well yes, but as you said, we could add a definition (or abbrev) AntisymmLE for this specialization, and this should still work with to_dual.
I guess that would be the solution with the least friction.

I was kinda hoping that docs#Digraph.toSimpleGraphStrict would use docs#AntisymmRel (or some new thing that also adds a ≠ b for irreflexivity), but I guess we could save those for new Relation.FooGen stuff, since the point of the file does seem to be about LE (judging by the module docstring).
Although I am surprised to see there's no IsPartialOrder α (Antisymmetrization α r) anywhere, only a bundled PartialOrder.

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

Well yes, but as you said, we could add a definition (or abbrev) AntisymmLE for this specialization, and this should still work with to_dual.

That would be my preference (modulo naming)
